content: Posaconazole oral suspension has significant interactions with various drugs due to its effect on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, as well as P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Below are the detailed interactions and clinical recommendations: 1. Midazolam (oral and intranasal): Posaconazole increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor closely. 2. Midostaurin: Posaconazole increases midostaurin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising the risk of adverse effects, especially during the first week of treatment. Avoid coadministration or monitor closely if necessary. 3. Mifepristone: Posaconazole increases mifepristone levels, necessitating a dose limit of 300 mg/day for Cushing syndrome when coadministered. This combination may also prolong the QT interval. Use alternatives if possible and monitor closely. 4. Mirtazapine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, and posaconazole further increases mirtazapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Mirvetuximab soravtansine: Posaconazole increases exposure to the cytotoxic component DM4, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Modafinil: Posaconazole increases modafinil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Mometasone (intranasal): Posaconazole increases mometasone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Montelukast: Posaconazole increases montelukast levels, but the clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 9. Moxifloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Naldemedine: Posaconazole increases naldemedine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein interaction, raising the risk of adverse effects. Monitor closely. 11. Naloxegol: Posaconazole significantly increases naloxegol levels, potentially causing opioid withdrawal symptoms. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Nefazodone: Posaconazole increases nefazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and nefazodone increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein interaction. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Nelfinavir: Posaconazole increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Neomycin (oral): Posaconazole decreases neomycin levels by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 15. Neratinib: Posaconazole increases neratinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 16. Netupitant/Palonosetron: Posaconazole increases netupitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. No dosage adjustment is required, but monitor closely. 17. Nevirapine: Posaconazole increases nevirapine levels, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Nicardipine: Posaconazole increases nicardipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and nicardipine increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein interaction. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Nifedipine: Posaconazole increases nifedipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, but nifedipine decreases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein interaction. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 20. Nilotinib: Posaconazole increases nilotinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and nilotinib increases posaconazole levels via P-glycoprotein interaction. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Nimodipine: Posaconazole increases nimodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 22. Nintedanib: Posaconazole increases nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein interaction. If adverse effects occur, consider dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation. Monitor closely. 23. Nirogacestat: Posaconazole increases nirogacestat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 24. Nisoldipine: Posaconazole increases nisoldipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Nitrendipine: Posaconazole increases nitrendipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 26. Nizatidine: Nizatidine decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Norgestrel: Posaconazole increases norgestrel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Nortriptyline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Octreotide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Olanzapine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Olaparib: Posaconazole increases olaparib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce olaparib dose and monitor closely. 33. Oliceridine: Posaconazole increases oliceridine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust oliceridine dosing and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 34. Olodaterol (inhaled): Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Omaveloxolone: Posaconazole increases omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or reduce omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day if unavoidable. Monitor closely. 36. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir: Posaconazole increases levels of this combination via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Omeprazole: Omeprazole decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Posaconazole increases omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Ondansetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and posaconazole increases ondansetron levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended in high-risk patients. 39. Osilodrostat: Posaconazole increases osilodrostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce osilodrostat dose by half and monitor closely. 40. Osimertinib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and posaconazole increases osimertinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 41. Ospemifene: Posaconazole increases ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Oxaliplatin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 43. Oxybutynin: Posaconazole increases oxybutynin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Oxycodone: Posaconazole increases oxycodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or reduce oxycodone dose. Monitor closely. 45. Ozanimod: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 46. Paclitaxel: Posaconazole increases paclitaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Pacritinib: Posaconazole increases pacritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Palbociclib: Posaconazole increases palbociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or reduce palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. Monitor closely. 49. Paliperidone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Palovarotene: Posaconazole increases palovarotene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 51. Panobinostat: Posaconazole increases panobinostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 52. Pantoprazole: Pantoprazole decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Parecoxib: Posaconazole increases parecoxib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown. 54. Paricalcitol: Posaconazole increases paricalcitol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Paromomycin: Posaconazole decreases paromomycin levels by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 56. Paroxetine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Pasireotide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 58. Pazopanib: Posaconazole increases pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or reduce pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. 59. Pemigatinib: Posaconazole increases pemigatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or reduce pemigatinib dose. Resume previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 60. Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 61. Pentobarbital: Pentobarbital decreases posaconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown. These interactions highlight the importance of careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or avoidance of coadministration to minimize adverse effects and ensure therapeutic efficacy.
